title.narrative: WGG- Feminist Leadership and Mentorship in Kenya

description.narrative: The objective of the strategy is to destabilise these structures by ensuring new women leaders are represented in policy and decision making spaces as well in convenings and conversations.

The program strategy aims to capacitate new women leaders, including WWDs and young women, on feminist leadership to build inclusive movements and alliances. The program recognises power structures, both visible and hidden, that exist within movements.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

(38) Out of the 20 Disability Champion trainined by the KNDW in 2022, 5 are engaged consistently in community level political processes; 6 girls and women were selected to be part of the Wangu Kanja GBV response Network, which is a network of rapid response GBV in mukuru that support women and girls to seek aid, medical and legal after an assault. Nyumba Kumi Initiative is an approach to policing that brings together the police, civil society and local communities to develop local solutions to safety and security concerns. Previously, women with disabilities were not taking part in these meetings both in Mukuru and Kibera. Women Spaces Africa capacitated women in Mukuru and Kibera in 2022/23. Follow up with those women with disabilities revealed that 21 women with disabilities were invited to take part in the Nyumba Kumi Initiative Meetings in Mukuru kwa Jenga slums while 18 women with disabilities have been attending the meetings consistently every month. One young woman with a disability has been absorbed into the GBV survivor network of Mukuru kwa Njenga for easier litigation purposes targetting women with disabilities. 2 women with disabilities have been absorbed as community health volunteers in Mukuru Kwa Njenga to assist with the specific needs of girls and women with disabilities.The targets that were submitted at the outset of the program were based on projected activities and results prior to all the work that went into building the WGG consoritum structure, which took a considerable amount of time, made further difficult by delays in funds transfer from MOFA to Consortium lead and from lead to subs. Building capacity of grassroots actors is both time and resource consuming and collectivising them for meaningful advocacy is more challenging than we anticipated.

40 Kenyan feminist leaders participated in FLMBaRI East Africa, strengthening leadership capacity and cross-regional movement engagement. This included representatives from Women Spaces Africa (WSA). Participation contributed to strengthening leadership pathways for women and girls with disabilities within feminist and political spaces.
